item.title: Re: Foundation 2.0
item.content:encoded: Thank you for the greenlight and useful critique! I realise that i need to work on the reason why the guard got sent into the parallel dimension, but I forgot to say that unless touched and their effect is activated, the villagers pay no heed to the guard, and almost nothing to what he does. I want to use this to show how he thinks hes at war at them and has an entire site going to to study and research, but no one else in the entire dimension cares or notices. I'm trying to create the sense of isolation, even in varied and unique company. As for his death, I'm trying to contrast the end of the journal as his crazed ravings are abruptly cut short by something very mundane, and even though he sees himself as a pioneer and his own site manager, he just trips over and falls down a small cliff, ending everything. He will then soberly read over his journal again and reflect on what he does, but not realising what happened to him and seriously believing he was a hero. I hope this makes sense to you.

item.title: Re: Foundation 2.0
item.content:encoded:
Interesting SCP you've got there!
Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Oooooh! Parrallel Dimensions? Sign me the heck up!
I'll be honest: I fricking love this idea. Trapped in a parallel world? The place you worked and loved and served for so long in ruins? Present in a place with no resemblance to your own world? No wonder he'd go insane! Oh, and the journal? Pure gold. I love it.
Although I do have a few concerns/suggestions:

  • Having him die in the end seems a bit out-of-place. Maybe have a series of transmissions he attempts to send to the foundation be the the last communication received from him? Leaving his actual ending ambiguous? Or maybe have him be hunted to death by the villagers?
  • The method used for teleportation is quite clever, although the entry of 507 and the guard into this dimension would need to be chaotic in some way. And the concept of D-Class attacking 507 for no reason seems a bit odd. I doubt there would be any D-Class just roaming around the Foundation. Maybe 507 and the guard could've been friends, and the guard was patting him on the shoulder/had his hand on 507's shoulder when walking down the hall? Something like that may seem a bit more plausible. Here's the original text of Addendum 507-00 for reference

When questioned, it said that ████ was holding onto its shoulder when it shifted, leading to both of them to appear in an alternate dimension where [EXPUNGED]. During the ensuing chaos, SCP-507 lost contact with ████ and could not relocate him before it shifted back into “standard” reality.

*Are the villagers really doing anything about the Guard being there? I get they're behaviorally/physiologically different from humans, but I still feel they should have a bit more of a role in the story. Otherwise, I feel there's a bit of lost potential.


Aside from that, this is a perfect concept, and I can't wait to see the final article! Here's your greenlight, and please do reach out if you have any questions/comments/concerns.

item.title: Foundation 2.0
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Tragedy, Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): A brief description and containment measures describing a parallel dimension which can be reached by some obscure ritual, and a village inside it, but story mainly told by a journal found by the foundation when they found out how to get inside. The foundation eventually leaves the dimension and doesn't return due to little reason to explore as the people and objects appear somewhat similar and they see no reason to take unnecessary risks.

Elevator Pitch: A foundation guard gets stuck in an alien dimension via contact with 507 when trying to break to break up a fight with a d class attacking them for some reason / the result of addemdum 507 - 00, and ends up in a parallel dimension with a village and villagers, that are similar to humans, but slightly behaviourally and physically different with a different language, and cause humans to disassociate from reality if continually touched

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The foundation later finds an obscure way into the dimension, and finds a journal and ruins of his base detailing his life. The agent steals from the villagers, and spies on them, trying to make proper files and dossiers on them, even making his own scp site, but eventually devolves into a cariacature of the foundation, capturing non - anomalous animals the he beleives are to study and make files on, as well as making overprecise and downright incorrect assumptions about the villagers in needless documents about their lives. He also tags the walls and trees with scp signs, and writes incoherent notes in his journal pertaining to enemies of the foundation and scps. He then breaks his leg and slowly dies because of sepsis, and reflects on what he did, and feels happy he contributed to the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How the guard loses his mind and becomes so obesessed with the foundation he forgets what it stands for and what it actually does, contain anomalies, and save humanity.

Additional Notes: I would like the journal to be somewhat comedic (eg: "gamers against weed are dumb little kids", "the goc is for nerds"), and make useless files on completely normal animals,
(e.g:
object class: keter
description: a rabbit i found, is anomalous but i dont know how yet
containment: a cage next to my bed
tests: eats carrots and shits occasionally), but I don't know if it would be funny enough/too meta/too much content

I'm new to this, so please correct me if anything stands out as off or out of place.
